Digital India

The Digital India programme was formally announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and launched on 1 July 2015 during Digital India Week, with the stated objective of bringing together multiple ICT initiatives under a single umbrella.
The government characterised it as a multi‑departmental, multi‑phase programme to be implemented in partnership with central ministries, state governments, industry, and civil society.

Over time, Digital India has evolved from primarily an e‑governance initiative to a broader digital public infrastructure (DPI) ecosystem built around digital identity, real‑time payments, electronic document storage, and consent‑based data sharing.
In later years, the government launched India Stack Global to present selected Indian digital platforms as exportable DPI models and to promote cooperation with other countries.
Governance and services on demand – including integrated and interoperable services, real‑time and paperless service delivery, online and mobile platforms, and digital grievance redressal.
Digital empowerment of citizens – including digital literacy, accessible digital resources in Indian languages, and participation in the digital economy and e‑governance.

The programme aims to improve internet connectivity, expand digital literacy, and increase access to electronic services as a means of supporting growth in digital services, electronics manufacturing, and employment, especially in rural and semi‑urban areas.

Some take issue with technological determinism, the notion that ICTs are a sure-fire antidote to the world's problems.
Instead, governments must adjust solutions to the specific political and social context of their nation.
Others note that technology amplifies underlying institutional forces, so technology must be accompanied by significant changes in policy and institutions to have a meaningful impact.
